nodes.description: The three missense alleles (p.Arg88Cys, p.Arg88His and p.His92Pro) alter conserved residues in a beta-hairpin loop of mL49 that forms part of its interface with the 16S rRNA in the large mitoribosomal subunit. The only other allele, a frameshift, occurred in trans to p.Arg88Cys. No homozygous loss-of-function allele has been observed, and the authors interpret the missense variants as hypomorphic: mL49 itself was reduced in patient fibroblasts, and complete loss is predicted to be lethal by analogy with other mitoribosomal large-subunit knockouts. The loop-to-rRNA interface is a structural model; no mL49 variant has been shown experimentally to break rRNA contact.

nodes.description: The tissues affected (cochlea, ovary, cerebral white matter and globus pallidus, retina, kidney) are energy-dependent tissues commonly hit in mitochondrial translation disorders. Why a given patient has some of these and not others is unexplained: the two families homozygous for p.His92Pro share a founder haplotype, yet one has Perrault syndrome and the other neither hearing loss nor ovarian failure. The authors propose an unidentified genetic modifier. MRPL49 protein was detected in mitochondria of mouse cochlear hair cells and supporting cells, which fits but does not explain the hearing phenotype.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from the two families tested had significantly less 16S rRNA than controls. Complexome profiling showed reduced large-subunit (about 60 and 70 percent lower) and small-subunit (about 15 and 40 percent lower) content, more marked in the more severely affected individual. Subunit components migrated normally and no assembly intermediates accumulated, so the authors propose reduced stability and degradation of the large subunit rather than an assembly block. Only two patient fibroblast lines have been studied.
